songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Alligator marathon, soaring leads, tight rhythm—high‑energy late‑'69 Dead show
ai_show_review.blurb: Features the epic Alligator > Caution > Feedback sequence alongside a blistering Eleven and Pigpen’s swagger on Good Morning Little School Girl. Jerry delivers crisp, soaring guitar tones while Phil’s bass drives the improvisations. The set flows from a blues‑heavy first half into an intense, seamless second‑set jam marathon.
ai_show_review.review: The Fillmore West on February 28, 1969 finds the Dead in top form, trading blistering blues for wild, exploratory flights that still feel fresh today. The first set builds momentum with tight renditions of Good Morning Little School Girl, Doin' That Rag and a fiery Turn On Your Lovelight, showcasing Pigpen’s vocal swagger and a rhythm section locked in lock‑step. Once the second set kicks off, the band launches into the classic Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cryptical sandwich before detonating into a monumental Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven chain that highlights Jerry’s soaring leads and Phil’s “bombing” bass lines. From there they barrel through Death Don't Have No Mercy into the legendary Alligator marathon, stitching Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks), Feedback and And We Bid You Good Night together without losing a beat. Across all three soundboard sources the performance is consistently high‑energy, with the multi‑track recording offering the clearest instrument separation to hear every nuance of this historic night.

best_recording.reason: Crisp multi‑track mix with excellent instrument separation, capturing the full detail of the Alligator suite despite minor pitch quirks.

Seamless Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven chain showcasing soaring leads and tight rhythm.

song_highlights: And We Bid You Good Night

band_performance.Jerry: Flows with inventive ideas all night; crisp tone on Lovelight, soaring leads on The Eleven and the Alligator suite, delivering a near‑perfect guitar performance.
band_performance.Phil: Bombs out bass lines that own the jams, especially on The Eleven and The Other One, providing a solid, driving foundation throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Solid rhythm work and vocal contributions keep the band grounded; his playing meshes tightly with Jerry’s leads.
band_performance.Mickey: Powerful drumming that fuels the high‑energy sections; minor speed/pitch wobble noted in the Alligator jam but overall performance remains strong.
band_performance.Billy: Provides a steady, propulsive beat alongside Mickey, anchoring the extended improvisations with reliable groove.
